about.title: Make everyday wallet use better, together
about.intro: imToken Fans brings wallet users together to share safety experiences, suggest improvements, discover community projects and discuss research and everyday use.
about.whyBody1: A question during a transfer, an easily missed safety tip or an idea for a smoother experience can all start a useful conversation.
about.whyBody2: Four sections connect safety stories, product collaboration, open discussion and community events, so you can find the right place to contribute.
about.makersBody: Tell a safety story, suggest a wallet improvement or share a tool you made. Community projects can use any technology.
about.membersBody: Add your use case, explain a confusing step, support a useful suggestion or join a research discussion.
about.relationshipBody1: This community is a place for imToken wallet users to exchange ideas. Authors are responsible for their posts; discussions do not automatically represent imToken’s official position.
about.relationshipBody2: Check the original source, publication date and relevant version when reading safety information or product announcements. Product decisions, event arrangements and rewards depend on their published terms.
about.relationshipNote: Nobody should ask you to share a recovery phrase, private key or password.
about.not1: Supporting a suggestion expresses demand and does not guarantee adoption.
about.not2: Market discussions and research reflect their authors’ views; use your own judgment.
about.not3: A community project listing is not an official endorsement or security certification.
about.not4: Participation requirements, dates and rewards depend on each event’s rules.
about.promiseBody: The four sections currently contain labeled demo content. Demo posts, comments and support stay in the current page state, without writing to the real community or earning XP or rewards. Live community features will be introduced in stages.

howItWorks.title: Find your section and start a useful conversation
howItWorks.intro: Start with a specific experience, question or idea. This guide explains where each kind of content belongs; the demo lets you explore the flow first.
howItWorks.maker1: Choose a section: safety stories in Wallet Safety, wallet issues in Product Feedback and tools in Community Projects.
howItWorks.maker2: Explain your goal, what happened and what help you are looking for.
howItWorks.maker3: Add relevant steps or screenshots after hiding addresses, balances and other sensitive information.
howItWorks.maker4: Respond to follow-up questions and add an update when the situation changes.
howItWorks.memberTitle: Four steps to joining a discussion
howItWorks.member1: Read the post and existing replies to understand the context.
howItWorks.member2: Add your own use case and distinguish experience from speculation.
howItWorks.member3: Support suggestions that matter to you and explain why they would help.
howItWorks.member4: Read published updates for progress; support counts do not promise adoption.
howItWorks.feedbackBody: Useful feedback can be short, as long as others can understand and investigate it.
howItWorks.feedback1: What were you trying to do?
howItWorks.feedback2: What happened, and how did it differ from your expectation?
howItWorks.feedback3: Can it be reproduced, and which version or device was involved?
howItWorks.feedback4: If it is a suggestion, when would it help?
howItWorks.followBody: The FAQ explains levels, XP, check-ins and prize draws using the current configuration. Interactions in demo sections do not grant XP or event rewards.
howItWorks.selectionBody: Browse the four sections, open demo posts and try local interactions. Live posting, feedback handling, video uploads and announcement publishing will be implemented in stages; this guide does not mean they are available yet.

guidelines.title: Share honestly and discuss respectfully
guidelines.intro: These guidelines apply to all four sections. Protect personal information, check your sources and respect other participants.
guidelines.principle1: Distinguish personal experience, cited information and your own interpretation. Include original sources.
guidelines.principle2: Discuss ideas and actions without personal attacks or mocking someone’s experience or technical skills.
guidelines.principle3: Choose the appropriate section, look for existing discussions and avoid spam or repeated advertising.
guidelines.principle4: Correct errors and label conclusions that still need verification.
guidelines.maker1: Give context, dates, events and verifiable sources for safety stories; do not spread attack materials that enable abuse.
guidelines.maker2: For suggestions, describe the goal, actual result and expectation. For projects, explain their stage, usage and known limitations.
guidelines.maker3: Disclose fees, sponsorship, team relationships or promotion instead of posing as an independent reviewer.
guidelines.maker4: Product announcements and feedback decisions require the relevant permissions; a verification label does not grant them.
guidelines.feedback1: Support suggestions based on real needs; do not coordinate fake votes or manipulate results with multiple accounts.
guidelines.feedback2: Provide verifiable steps and relevant details instead of substituting insults for an issue description.
guidelines.feedback3: Distinguish facts, analysis and predictions in research and market discussions; do not promise returns or solicit copy trading.
guidelines.feedback4: Do not publish private conversations, identities, transaction records or other personal information without permission.
guidelines.notAllowed1: Recovery phrases, private keys, passwords, verification codes or screenshots exposing sensitive personal information.
guidelines.notAllowed2: Phishing links, malware or impersonation of support staff or official representatives.
guidelines.notAllowed3: Scams, guaranteed returns, fake airdrops or requests for payment to unlock rewards.
guidelines.notAllowed4: Plagiarized or infringing material, unauthorized internal documents or private information.
guidelines.notAllowed5: Hate, harassment, repeated spam or unlawful content.
guidelines.moderationBody1: Moderation follows the system’s available capabilities and operating rules. These content standards do not mean the new sections’ moderation flows are live.
guidelines.moderationBody2: Stop interacting with suspicious content and use an available report control. For account or asset risks, seek help through a verifiable official channel.
guidelines.disclaimerBody: Community discussions are not investment advice, project listings are not official endorsements, and support does not guarantee adoption. Event participation, prizes and delivery follow the event’s published rules.

forMakers.title: Tell the story behind your experience or project
forMakers.intro: Whether you are sharing an experience or a tool you built, help readers understand the problem it addresses.
forMakers.fitBody: Start with something you know and choose the section that fits.
forMakers.fit1: Wallet Safety: real cases, risk awareness, lessons learned and everyday precautions.
forMakers.fit2: Product Co-creation: imToken issues, improvement suggestions and community-built tools or products, with no AI requirement.
forMakers.fit3: General Discussion and Events: research, market discussions and community topics; check the organizer and rules for events.
forMakers.pageBody: Give readers enough context without repeated follow-up questions.
forMakers.page1: Summarize the issue or value of your project in one sentence.
forMakers.page2: Describe the audience, use case and current version or stage.
forMakers.page3: Include relevant steps, screenshots or sources, with sensitive information hidden.
forMakers.page4: Say what help you need, and disclose fees or commercial relationships.
forMakers.questionBody: “Which part of this approval message is confusing?” is easier to answer usefully than “What do you think?”
forMakers.updateTitle: Add an update when things change
forMakers.updateBody: If an issue is resolved, a project changes or a conclusion is revised, add the date, details and applicable version. The demo does not publish live release notes.
forMakers.responseBody: Understand the other person’s context before explaining your view. Mark unverified information as uncertain.
forMakers.statusBody: Submitting a suggestion or receiving support does not mean adoption. Handling decisions and formal announcements require authorized publishers.
forMakers.not1: Do not upload recovery phrases, private keys, passwords or personal information without permission.
forMakers.not2: Do not fabricate experiences, reviews, official verification or commitments.
forMakers.not3: Do not replace useful content with profit promises, manipulated votes or repeated advertising.

forTesters.title: Your real experience makes discussion useful
forTesters.intro: You do not need a technical background to contribute a specific question, experience or reliable source.
forTesters.chooseTitle: Start with what matters to you
forTesters.chooseBody: Visit Wallet Safety for practical lessons, Product Co-creation for wallet improvements, General Discussion for research and markets, and Events for community activities.
forTesters.feedbackBody: Describe what happened without drawing conclusions for others.
forTesters.feedback1: Your goal and the context of your actions.
forTesters.feedback2: The step that blocked you, the actual result and your expected result.
forTesters.feedback3: Relevant version information, reproduction steps or redacted screenshots.
forTesters.feedback4: The impact of the issue and the improvement you would find useful.
forTesters.discloseBody: Say when you have not personally used something. Disclose if you are its author, a team member or paid to discuss it.
forTesters.safetyBody: Hide wallet addresses, balances and personal information before sharing. Never provide recovery phrases, private keys or passwords, or send money to strangers to join a discussion.
forTesters.reputationBody: Helpful contributions matter more than repeated replies. Real XP and levels follow the current rules in the FAQ; sample levels and demo interactions do not affect your account.
forTesters.rewardBody: Trying a project, supporting an idea or joining a discussion does not automatically earn rewards, airdrops or a commitment to adopt a suggestion. Event rewards depend on the event’s rules.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.subtitle: Learn how to participate and what the demo covers, then explore existing level, XP and activity rules.
faq.xpIntro: XP determines your community level. Besides checking in and drawing at the <activitiesLink>activity centre</activitiesLink>, these everyday actions earn XP:
faq.xpAllDisabled: The team has temporarily disabled every way of earning XP.
faq.xpNote1: · "Up to N per day" is an anti-farming cap that resets at midnight Beijing time.
faq.xpNote2: · Each object counts once: the same comment, votes on the same submission, a simulated investment in the same project — repeats don't earn again.
faq.xpNote3: · When content is deleted or rejected, the XP it earned is revoked; restoring and republishing it gives the XP back.
faq.levelsIntro: There are {max} levels, topping out at Lv{max} "{topTier}". Your level badge shows next to your name — in comments, on hover cards and on submission pages. Your own <profileLink>profile</profileLink> shows the XP bar and how much is left to the next level; other people only see your level and total XP. You get an in-app notification when you level up.
faq.checkinIntro: A cycle is {cycle} consecutive days, with the big prize on day {bigDay}. Finish a cycle and it loops back to day 1. Miss a day and the streak resets to day 1. A full cycle is worth {total} XP.
faq.checkinIntroNoBigDay: A cycle is {cycle} consecutive days. Finish a cycle and it loops back to day 1. Miss a day and the streak resets to day 1. A full cycle is worth {total} XP.
faq.checkinTimezone: A "day" follows Beijing time (UTC+8); the next check-in unlocks at midnight.
faq.lotteryCost: · Each draw costs {tickets} ticket(s). With no tickets the draw button is disabled; your current balance is shown right under it.
faq.lotteryCostWithXp: · Each draw costs {tickets} ticket(s) plus {xp} XP. With no tickets the draw button is disabled; your current balance is shown right under it.
faq.lotterySource: · Tickets are granted by the team (campaigns, compensation and so on).
faq.lotterySourceWithTicketPrize: · Tickets are granted by the team (campaigns, compensation and so on), and the grid itself has a "tickets" prize — winning it is a free extra spin.
faq.lotteryOdds: · Odds are computed live from prize weights. When a limited prize runs out, its share is spread across the rest. The live numbers are in "Prizes & odds" on the activity page.
faq.lotteryDelivery: · XP and badge prizes land instantly; physical prizes are arranged by the team.
faq.lotteryDrawsPerDay: · Up to {count} draws per day, resetting at midnight Beijing time.
faq.lotteryWindow: · This run: {start} — {end}. No draws outside that window.
faq.badgesIntro: Badges come in two kinds: automatic achievements (granted by the system once you qualify) and official honours (granted manually by admins). Badges appear on your profile and hover card.
faq.submissionsNote1: · Only products can be submitted. Product links are checked for duplicates before manual review. Historical ideas remain available to browse and interact with; new idea submissions are closed.
faq.submissionsNote2: Live section posting, feedback handling, support votes and video file uploads are still to be implemented.
faq.submissionsNote3: · Products use separate support votes and 1–5 star experience ratings. Ideas keep the "would pay" and "very creative" votes.
faq.submissionsNote4: Level, XP, check-in and prize draw values on this page come from the existing configuration. Participation depends on each activity’s current status and rules.

comments.first: This is a specific starting point. Describing exactly where the confusion happens makes it easier to keep the conversation useful.
comments.second: I wonder how people with different experience would understand it. We could keep a few alternatives and compare them together.
comments.reply: Agreed. Let’s describe the problem clearly before exploring solutions.
comments.note1: Perhaps we could start with one concrete situation and see where people get stuck.
comments.note2: Clear sources would help readers check the details afterward.
comments.note3: It would be useful to compare perspectives from people with different experience.
comments.note4: Collecting questions first, then making a short checklist, could help the discussion.
comments.note5: I wonder whether this is just as easy to read on a phone.
comments.note6: Keeping the context would make later contributions more useful.

approval-checklist.title: Three questions I ask before reviewing approvals
approval-checklist.excerpt: Understand why an approval exists, whether it is still needed, and what remains unclear before acting.
approval-checklist.body1: My fictional checklist asks: which interaction created this approval, do I still need it, and do I understand its purpose? No personal wallet information belongs in the discussion.
approval-checklist.body2: When something is unclear, I mark it for verification rather than following a blanket suggestion to remove everything. Different applications have different requirements.
approval-checklist.body3: What would you add to a community checklist? Use fictional scenarios and hide sensitive information in any images.
approval-checklist.poll: What should a checklist explain first?

clearer-transaction.title: A small suggestion: make transaction confirmations easier to read
clearer-transaction.excerpt: Put important information first and explain unfamiliar terms in plain language.
clearer-transaction.body1: Imagine a user wanting to understand an action before reviewing its parameters. Putting the essentials first could make that moment easier to navigate.
clearer-transaction.body2: The action, the parties involved, and important cautions could have distinct layers. Keep the first explanation short and make extra context available when needed.
clearer-transaction.body3: The illustration is for discussing information hierarchy. Which part would you change first? I would also like to hear how someone using a wallet for the first time would read it.

first-wallet-question.title: Which concept would you learn first when starting with wallets?
first-wallet-question.excerpt: Addresses, networks, approvals: I would like a learning framework that can grow one question at a time.
first-wallet-question.body1: With so many unfamiliar words, it is difficult to know which ideas to understand first and which to explore in context. I would like to hear how others began learning.
first-wallet-question.body2: I prefer learning one concept and explaining it in my own words. If the explanation requires many more unfamiliar terms, I probably need another pass.
first-wallet-question.body3: There is no need to share assets or activity records. Share a learning sequence or a sample question that would help a newcomer.
first-wallet-question.poll: How do you prefer to learn?

weekend-conversation.title: Weekend conversation room: bring one question
weekend-conversation.excerpt: An activity concept where a small group turns everyday confusion into questions everyone can understand.
weekend-conversation.body1: This is a fictional proposal, not an event registration notice. Imagine a half-hour session where people describe one question and others first ask for clarification.
weekend-conversation.body2: The focus is understanding, not inspecting wallets. It would not require screen sharing or collecting sensitive information. Complex topics could become future learning notes.
weekend-conversation.body3: Any real event would need a separate schedule and participation rules. This post explores the format and promises no places or rewards.

fake-support-message.title: An unexpected support message is a reason to pause
fake-support-message.excerpt: Verify the source independently. An urgent private message is not a reason to share sensitive information.
fake-support-message.body1: Fictional case: a user receives an unsolicited message claiming to be support and demanding immediate verification. Familiar-looking names and avatars do not establish identity.
fake-support-message.body2: I would stop the conversation and find a trusted source independently. I would never share a seed phrase, private key, or password, or follow an unfamiliar verification request.
fake-support-message.body3: When discussing similar experiences, remove identifying details and unsafe links. Share the recognition process without spreading clickable suspicious addresses.
fake-support-message.poll: Which topic would help you most?

ai-explainer.title: Chain Bookmarks: a concept for organizing useful resources
ai-explainer.excerpt: Organize resources by network and purpose, without connecting a wallet or reading assets. A concept, with no available product yet.
ai-explainer.body1: Chain Bookmarks is a fictional build created to demonstrate this community section. No real product is available. Its creator, features and support count are examples, with no official imToken product relationship.
ai-explainer.body2: Imagine a resource folder saved on your device: manually add titles, purposes and source notes, then organize them by network or topic. No wallet connection, address or asset history is needed. Users must still check whether a link is trustworthy.
ai-explainer.body3: This example illustrates discovery, support, creator discussion and iteration. Try local support or comments below; refreshing resets them. There is no live trial link, and supporting is not counted as a completed trial.
ai-explainer.poll: Which organizing feature would you try first?

reading-release-notes.title: Product update draft: make release notes easier to read
reading-release-notes.excerpt: A fictional announcement layout, with no actual release or official publication.
reading-release-notes.body1: This fictional sample demonstrates the product updates section through a made-up author. It has no real version, release date or official publisher identity, and announces no actual imToken change.
reading-release-notes.body2: A useful update can explain the change and its impact, then describe scope, precautions and a verifiable original source. Real announcements will require an authorized publisher to confirm the version and source.
reading-release-notes.body3: An announcement can link to processed feedback for context. Publishing it should not automatically mark every linked item as complete. This page only demonstrates reading and discussion, without changing statuses.
reading-release-notes.poll: What matters most in update notes?

learning-notebook.title: A learning notebook: question, source, next step
learning-notebook.excerpt: Turn saved links into knowledge you can explain, starting with three simple columns.
learning-notebook.body1: I give each question its own row: what I want to understand, where the information came from, and what still needs checking. This makes it easier to see what I actually learned.
learning-notebook.body2: After reading, I close the source and try to explain the idea. If something is unclear, I revisit that question instead of endlessly saving more links.
learning-notebook.body3: The same structure could support community notes. Keep observations and interpretations separate, and leave unverified parts as questions.

checkin-routine.title: A check-in can be a gentle reason to revisit a conversation
checkin-routine.excerpt: I would rather find something worth reading than feel obliged to press a daily button.
checkin-routine.body1: Some people prefer a routine; others return with a question. Both approaches are useful, and neither needs pressure from a streak.
checkin-routine.body2: On a visit, choose a conversation that interests you and decide whether to reply. Existing check-in and lucky draw pages have their own actual rules.
checkin-routine.body3: I prefer reminders with a frequency I can control: quiet when I am busy, useful when a conversation interests me. What would feel natural to you?
checkin-routine.poll: How would you prefer to return?

network-help.title: An unfamiliar network name: how can I ask a clear question?
network-help.excerpt: Describe what you saw and what you intended to do before sharing an unedited screenshot.
network-help.body1: I would describe the visible message, the intended action, and the last clear step before the confusion. That gives others more to work with than simply saying something does not work.
network-help.body2: There is no need to share an address, balance, seed phrase, or private key. If an image helps, hide sensitive information and keep only the relevant part.
network-help.body3: A community reply can help clarify concepts. Verify any concrete action through trusted material instead of following unsolicited private messages.
network-help.poll: What should a help template explain first?

better-questions.title: Before discussing a trend, I ask what problem it solves
better-questions.excerpt: Putting a new term in a concrete context may be more useful than rushing to a conclusion.
better-questions.body1: When I encounter a popular concept, I first try to describe one use case and compare it with an existing approach. A concrete question can make an abstract term much easier to discuss.
better-questions.body2: Separate observable behavior, a team’s stated goal, and our own assumptions. Mark unsupported parts for verification so the discussion can improve over time.
better-questions.body3: Share a questioning framework if you have one. There is no need for price predictions or asset figures to support a perspective.

reading-circle.title: Activity proposal: explain one wallet term in your own words
reading-circle.excerpt: A text-based learning concept with no prizes and no requests for wallet information.
reading-circle.body1: Each person could choose a term and explain it in a short paragraph. Others could point out unclear wording and help improve it. There is no real registration or confirmed schedule here.
reading-circle.body2: Examples can be entirely fictional. The focus is understanding and expression. Do not submit wallet screenshots or suggest one approach fits everyone.
reading-circle.body3: Any future event would need separately confirmed arrangements. For now, would you prefer rewriting one shared term together or choosing something you recently learned?
reading-circle.poll: Which learning format appeals to you?
reading-circle.option2: A term chosen by each person

simulation.title: Preview asset changes before signing a transfer
simulation.description:
Before confirming a transaction, I would like to see what leaves my wallet, what arrives, and the estimated fee.
Checking asset changes would help when using an exchange service for the first time. This IDEA and its status are fictional.

preview.title: Simulate balance changes on the transaction confirmation screen
preview.description: Show balances before and after a transfer or swap on the signing screen, reducing manual checks. This is similar to the asset preview IDEA and can be used to try merging.

addresses.title: Add labels and groups for frequent recipient addresses
addresses.description: Label addresses for family and frequent recipients, and make them easy to find across networks to reduce copying mistakes.

permissions.title: View and manage DApp approvals in one place
permissions.description: See approved DApps in one place, filter by network, and clearly display approval scopes. This is only a progress example and does not revoke real approvals.

networks.title: Remember my scroll position after switching networks
networks.description: Remember where I was in the asset list when browsing different networks so I can continue on return. The Complete status is only a board example.

comments.scenario: Showing token amounts and fees together before a swap would help, especially when using a DApp for the first time.
comments.reply: Which information would you like to see first? For example, outgoing amounts, estimated receipts and fees.
comments.preview: I would also like to see balances before and after a transfer. This comment comes from the other similar IDEA.
